assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a new boson with the properties of the Standard Model Higgs, completing the electroweak sector predicted decades earlier, is a clear, concrete discovery in nature and not a model-dependent interpretation. It is among the most consequential experimental results in fundamental physics, and as a theorist I value that it tests the mechanism of mass generation directly.
assessment.attribution: The discovery rests on two collaborations of several thousand people, so any prize must choose individuals. Jenni (ATLAS) and Virdee (CMS) are long-standing founders and leaders of the two experiments, and Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of the announcement. Della Negra is an equally credible founder of CMS. I would pick one proposal from each experiment plus the spokesperson of the discovery period, but this is a judgment about leadership rather than individual scientific authorship.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: the 2012 observation has been confirmed independently by both experiments with many decay channels, and the coupling measurements are now precise. The 2013 prize recognised the theory, so the experimental side is a long-standing open recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the statutes' three-person limit can fairly represent two large collaborations.
Whether leadership roles map onto decisive scientific contribution; my reading of the individual roles relies on recollection and I have not verified it.
Choosing between Della Negra and Virdee, or between Jenni and Gianotti, is difficult without detailed knowledge of the internal histories.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, followed by their observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened a new class of quantum matter classified by topology rather than symmetry breaking. The concept is original, clear and has spawned a very wide field, from topological semimetals to protected edge transport.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the decisive theoretical insight (the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall proposal). Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation, building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not in the credited names. This makes the three-name configuration appealing, but the theory side of the credit (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, also Fu) is contested and cannot be repaired from this list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across multiple materials and probes since 2005-2007, including three-dimensional topological insulators. The core effect is stable; the practical applications are still modest, but the conceptual impact is established and the timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) lies outside the credited names and could weaken a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio.
Overlap with the Haldane 2016 prize on topological phases may reduce the perceived novelty for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter, and a tunable platform where strongly correlated physics can be explored. It is original and extremely influential.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 theoretical prediction of the magic angle. Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery, together with the first author Yuan Cao. The proposal is clean in structure (theory plus experiment), though the exclusion of students and of other contributors (for example the earlier work on twisted layers) is a matter I cannot settle.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years from the experimental discovery; reproduced by many groups with a rich phase diagram. The microscopic nature of the superconductivity is still debated, which makes the interpretive part less mature than the existence of the flat-band phenomenon, but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is not settled, so recognition may be seen as early.
Credit for related earlier theoretical work on twisted bilayers (not in the list) may be raised by other members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of the magic wavelength lattice clock and its realisation with strontium and ytterbium atoms brought optical clocks to the 10^-18 level of fractional uncertainty, with direct applications in tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a future redefinition of the second. The idea is original and conceptually simple.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, and Ye's group pushed its accuracy and precision to the frontier. This is a natural two-person pairing; it is not clear that further individuals (for example in the ion-clock community or Hall and Hansch's frequency-comb work, already recognised in 2005) should be added.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: several independent labs have reached very high accuracy with lattice clocks, and international comparison campaigns are underway. Recognition is timely, with the redefinition of the second planned.
uncertainties: The overlap with the 2005 prize on laser-based precision spectroscopy and frequency combs and the 2012 prize on controlled quantum systems could be viewed as incremental by some.
Relative weight of the lattice proposal versus the demonstration of record accuracy is unclear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered the first full-sky, high-precision measurement of CMB anisotropies, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the Universe to percent level and establishing the standard cosmological model. As a cosmologist-theorist I regard this as the observational foundation that makes quantitative statements about dark energy and inflationary initial conditions possible.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the WMAP mission as principal investigator, Page was a principal designer of the instrument and the early analysis, and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. The credit is plausible, but a large team contributed, and the roles of Wilkinson and others are historically important.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: independent confirmation from Planck and ground-based experiments. The Planck mission arguably supersedes WMAP in precision, and the Nobel prize 2006 for COBE and 2019 prize for physical cosmology already cover related ground, which lowers its distinctiveness.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers WMAP or Planck as the representative of CMB precision mapping.
Whether previous cosmology prizes (2006 and 2019) leave room for another CMB-based award.
The Hubble tension and other anomalies do not affect the core result but may complicate the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of the shadows of M87* and Sgr A* are a direct visual confirmation of strong-gravity predictions and of the existence of event-horizon-scale compact objects. This speaks to my own interests in black holes and quantum gravity, even if the images are mainly a test of classical general relativity.
assessment.attribution: The credit is difficult. Doeleman led the EHT as director and developed the VLBI technique; Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept and chaired the science council; Zensus led the MPIfR contributions and the collaboration board. The project involved over 200 people, so any three-person configuration is a coarse reflection of a collective achievement.
assessment.maturity: Results from 2019 and 2022 are confirmed in later epochs, but the interpretation of the ring size to constrain gravity is limited by model dependence, and the spin and jet details are still evolving. Recognition is arguably still early.
uncertainties: Large collaboration and ambiguity over who made decisive contributions, with the 2020 prize for black-hole theory and observation (Penrose, Genzel, Ghez) also relevant.
Dependence of the tests of general relativity on astrophysical modelling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84) and entanglement-based quantum cryptography (Ekert) established that the laws of quantum mechanics can guarantee secure communication, and were seminal for quantum information science. The idea is original, clear and has led to real-world networks and satellite links.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84, and Ekert independently proposed the entanglement-based protocol in 1991. This is a natural three-person set. Wiesner's earlier unpublished conjugate-coding idea is a relevant historical contribution that cannot be credited here.
assessment.maturity: The protocols are mature and have been implemented in fibre and via satellite; however the 2022 prize on entanglement experiments already recognised closely related foundations, and real-world security (device-independence) is still under development.
uncertainties: Possible proximity to the 2022 prize on entangled photons may limit enthusiasm.
Wiesner's role in the origin of conjugate coding is outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal for quantum computation with trapped ions by Cirac and Zoller, combined with experimental realisation of gates and algorithms with ion traps by Blatt, set the template for controlled-atom quantum information processing and simulation. It is a very significant achievement at the intersection of theory and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposals, and Blatt (with others such as Wineland, already recognised, and Monroe, not in the list) led key experiments. Bloch's contribution relates to optical lattice simulation and might be better treated in a separate prize; I would limit a prize to the ion-trap line to keep a coherent discovery.
assessment.maturity: The ion-trap proposal dates from 1995 and has been confirmed repeatedly; trapped-ion quantum computers are a leading platform. Timing is good, but the 2012 prize for Wineland and Haroche covers part of the territory.
uncertainties: The candidate bundles ions, neutral atoms and quantum simulation, which may make a single coherent prize difficult.
Overlap with the 2012 prize and the possibility that other platform leaders (for example Monroe) deserve credit.
